summary: An L-4 ground house built in 1952 to replace a 1930 lookout, staffed into the mid-1980s, restored in 1995, and now a rentable NRHP-listed cabin.

facts.design: L-4 (hip-roof, 1936 standard model, ground house with catwalk)

access.note: Part of Forest Service cabin rental program on the Lolo National Forest.

facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service, Lolo National Forest

events.note: First lookout: an L-4 cab with gable roof.
Present hip-roof L-4 ground house with catwalk built, replacing the 1930 structure.
Last regularly staffed in the mid-1980s (exact year not specified by sources).
Passport in Time volunteer project reroofed the lookout and replaced/repaired windows and door.
Added to the National Historic Lookout Register, April 24, 2009.

evidence.supports: 1952 structure is only standard hip-roof L-4 ground house on the Lolo
evidence.quote: The current Cougar Peak lookout, built in 1952, is the only standard 1936-model hip-roof L-4 ground house with catwalk on the Lolo National Forest.
This structure replaced an L-4 cab with gable roof built in 1930.

evidence.supports: staffed into mid-1980s and rental program
evidence.quote: Cougar was last regularly staffed in the mid-1980's, and is currently on the cabin rental program.

evidence.supports: rock art left by former lookouts, earliest 1921
evidence.quote: The earliest rock inscription is dated 1921, surrounded by numerous other rock carvings of names, dates, and artwork by lookouts of the past.
A 1995 Passport in Time project saw the reroofing of the lookout, and the replacing and repairing of windows and the door, as well as other repairs.
First established in 1930 with an L-4 cab, the present L-4 cab replaced it in 1952.

evidence.supports: Clyde Fickes association and period of significance
evidence.quote: Fickes, Clyde ... Periods Of Significance: 1952 AD - 1967 AD
